[element-xref]
=== `<xref>` X(cross) Reference

Reference to an object within the standards document (for example, a table, a bibliographic citation, a figure).

#### Usage/Remarks
This element may be used to reference anything that has an attribute of type <<attribute-id,`@id`>>.
##### Best Practice

The <<attribute-ref-type,`@ref-type`>> attribute (of the <<element-xref,`<xref>`>> element) can be used to preserve information concerning what type of element is being pointed to by the cross-reference.
#### Accessibility

Sometimes a `<xref>` needs to be pronounced in a way that is not reflected in its content or its tagging. The <<attribute-alt,`@alt`>> attribute can be used to record the pronunciation for screen readers and other accessibility devices. For example, a cross-reference to a figure might be pronounced as “Figure 4”.
##### Custom Type of Reference (<<attribute-ref-type,`@ref-type`>>)

The <<attribute-ref-type,`@ref-type`>> attribute can be used to preserve information concerning the type of element that is the target of the cross-reference (for example, a figure (“`fig`”), a table (“`table`”), or a footnote (“`fn`”)). <<attribute-ref-type,`@ref-type`>> has as its values a fixed list of types. If your object is not one of the listed types, you can use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to describe the actual type. Set the value of <<attribute-ref-type,`@ref-type`>> to “`custom`” and also use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to hold any object type you require. For example:
[source,xml]
....
<xref ref-type="custom" custom-type="glossary".../>
... <xref ref-type="custom" custom-type="term".../>
....
